questions.q: Where did Yahweh tell Moses and Aaron that the tribes must set up their tents?
questions.a: Yahweh told them that each tribe must camp near its own banner and the sign of its ancestral family. They must camp around the tent of meeting, at a distance from it.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh say the 74,600 men of the army of the tribe of Judah must camp, and who must lead their army?
questions.a: They must camp near the banner of Judah on the east side of the tent of meeting, where the sun rises, and Nahshon must lead their army.

questions.q: Where must the 54,400 men of the tribe of Issachar camp, and who must lead their army?
questions.a: They must camp next to Judah, and Nethanel must lead their army.

questions.q: Where must the 57,400 men of the tribe of Zebulun camp, and who must lead their army?
questions.a: They must also camp next to Judah, and Eliab must lead their army.

questions.q: Who must set out first from the camp?
questions.a: The whole camp of Judah, with the two tribes that set up their tents near Judah tribe, must set out first.

questions.q: Where must the 46,500 men of the tribe of Reuben camp, and who must lead their army?
questions.a: They must camp near the banner of Reuben on the south side of the tent of meeting, and Elizur must lead their army.

questions.q: Where must the 59,300 men of the tribe of Simeon camp, and who must lead their army?
questions.a: They must camp next to Reuben, and Shelumiel must lead their army.

questions.q: Where must the 45,650 men of the tribe of Gad camp, and who must lead their army?
questions.a: They must also camp next to Reuben, and Eliasaph must lead their army.

questions.q: Who must set out second from the camp?
questions.a: The whole camp of Reuben, with the two tribes that set up their tents near Reuben tribe, must set out second.

questions.q: Where will the tent of meeting and the camp of the Levites be when they set out?
questions.a: They will be in the midst of the camps.

questions.q: Where must the 40,500 men of the tribe of Ephraim camp, and who must lead their army?
questions.a: They must camp near the banner of Ephraim on the west side of the tent of meeting, and Elishama must lead their army.

questions.q: Where must the 32,200 men of the tribe of Manasseh camp, and who must lead their army?
questions.a: They must camp next to Ephraim, and Gamaliel must lead their army.

questions.q: Where must the 35,400 men of the tribe of Benjamin camp, and who must lead their army?
questions.a: They must also camp next to Ephraim, and Abidan must lead their army.

questions.q: How many men are counted in the camp of Ephraim?
questions.a: The camp of Ephraim has 108,100 men.

questions.q: When must the camp of Ephraim set out in relation to the other camps?
questions.a: The camp of Ephraim must set out third.

questions.q: Who leads the tribe of Dan?
questions.a: Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai leads the tribe of Dan.

questions.q: How many men are counted in the army of the tribe of Dan?
questions.a: The army of the tribe of Dan has 62,700 men.

questions.q: Where must the 41,500 men of the tribe of Asher camp, and who must lead their army?
questions.a: They must camp next to Dan, and Pagiel must lead their army.

questions.q: Where must the 53,400 men of the tribe of Naphtali camp, and who must lead their army?
questions.a: They must also camp next to Dan, and Ahira must lead their army.

questions.q: Who must set out last from the camp?
questions.a: The whole camp of Dan, with the two tribes that set up their tents near Dan tribe, must set out last, and the men there number 157,600.

questions.q: Whom did Moses and Aaron not count among the people of Israel, and why?
questions.a: They did not count the Levites among the people of Israel because Yahweh had commanded Moses not to count them.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel do?
questions.a: The people of Israel did everything that Yahweh commanded Moses. They camped by their banners, and they set out by their clans and their ancestral families.

commentary.text: The order of the tribes in their tents.

—The tribes were to encamp about the tabernacle, which was to be in the midst of them. It was a token of God's gracious presence. Yet they were to pitch their tents afar off, in reverence to the sanctuary. The children of Israel put themselves in their posts, without murmuring or disputing; and as it was their safety, so it was their beauty. It is our duty and interest to be contented with the place allotted to us, and to endeavour to occupy it in a proper manner, without envying or murmuring; without ambition or covetousness. Thus the gospel church ought to be compact, according to the Scripture model, every one knowing and keeping his place; and then all that wish well to the church rejoice, beholding their order, Col 2:5.
